citation.title: Overview and recent progress of KSTAR diagnostics
citation.authors: S.G. Lee, Y.U. Nam, J.G. Bak, J.W. Juhn, J.H. Lee, K.D. Lee, S.H. Seo, W.H. Ko, J.S. Ko, J. Lee, W.C. Lee, J.H. Kim, J. Jang and KSTAR team

topic: Descriptive overview of the KSTAR diagnostic suite, including CES, ECEI, Thomson, ECE, reflectometry and MSE, and of real-time diagnostic needs.
own_question: Summarize the progress and future plans of KSTAR diagnostics.
actual_method_and_evidence: A narrative review with example figures. No figures were visually checked here. The CES text describes carbon-impurity Ti and toroidal rotation at 10 ms time resolution. It mentions a modulated neutral beam used for background subtraction and 32 fibers covering core to edge. It also notes that CES Ti profiles have been used to classify L- and H-mode plasmas. ECEI is described qualitatively, covering optics flexibility and correlation analysis. BES is not described. Real-time needs are stated as requirements and plans: future FPGA feedback and long-pulse capability up to 300 s.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: KSTAR CES measures carbon-impurity ion temperature and toroidal rotation profiles with a stated 10 ms time resolution, using modulated-beam background subtraction.
claim_checks.qualification: This is impurity Ti, not main-ion Ti. The 10 ms figure is a time resolution, not a report latency or arrival time. The configuration may differ for the 2022 chord we use.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: KSTAR's steady-state long-pulse mission motivates diagnostics that deliver reliable real-time data integrated into control.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a stated requirement and plan, not demonstrated real-time CES or a demonstrated nowcasting benefit.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: The source gives a CES time resolution of 10 ms. It does not report CES report arrival times or processing latency.
validation_if_relevant: Not applicable. The source contains no predictive validation.
forbidden_inferences: CES reports are available online within 10 ms
CES yields main-ion or electron temperature
The source describes BES or supports BES-based Ti inference
ECEI wavenumber limits apply to our 10 ms voltage snapshots
Planned FPGA real-time capability exists for CES
CES labels are independent physical truth
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include as a citable descriptor of the KSTAR CES (carbon impurity, 10 ms) and of the real-time control motivation. It is not evidence of latency or of predictive performance.
